title: sequence-length-decay-model-driven-kernel-cascade
creator: Nora Diaz
description:
Summary: Build and validate a kernel selection subsystem that uses learned sequence-length decay profiles + multi-fidelity probes to pick a compact cascade of kernels (fast-but-specialized → fallback-general) per-model and per-request-trajectory. Goal is reduce tail latency and token cost across variable-length production traffic without regressing quality.

Motivation: Current single-shot kernel pickers struggle with high variance in seq-length trajectories (short bursts then long continuations) and either over-optimise for median or pay heavy tail latency. By modeling the expected remaining token distribution (a.k.a. 'decay profile') at prefill and during decode, we can select a short cascade of kernels: a low-latency kernel for the likely short remainder, a mid-range kernel for average continuations, and an accuracy-preserving fallback. This avoids expensive probing at every decision point and allows warm-started kernels for decode checkpoints.

Scope and deliverables:
- Implement a lightweight decay-profile estimator: histogram + exponential-fit per model version trained from recent traffic and eval traces.
- Multi-fidelity probe harness: microbench probes (fast) + 1-2 full-payload probes (slow) used offline to seed kernel utility priors.
- Kernel cascade policy: select top-2 kernels by expected cost*P(remain small) + latency risk term; include deterministic safety fallback when KPIs cross thresholds.
- Prefill integration: compute initial decay estimate from prompt length, model policy, and cached user/session fingerprints; produce initial cascade choice and warm-start KV cache for chosen kernels.
- Runtime: fast in-request selector that can switch mid-decode at checkpoint boundaries with minimal KV-copy overhead.
- Metrics + dashboards: per-request cascade chosen, tail p95/p99 latency, token cost delta, quality regression flags (ROUGE/API-based), and rollout gating.

Success criteria:
- 10–18% reduction in p99 generation latency for workloads with mixed short+long sequences (internal benchmark set A).
- <= 2% quality regression on anchor prompt set; immediate rollback on any regression above 0.5% on critical prompts.
- No more than 3% increase in median latency for strictly long-only workloads.

Technical approach details:
1) Decay model: maintain per-model-version two simple representations: (a) a 16-bin histogram of observed remaining-lengths conditioned on observed prefix length buckets, updated with exponential decay; (b) a single-parameter exponential decay fit per prefix bucket used for quick expectation calculation. Both are small (<= 1KB per model-version).
2) Multi-fidelity probing: offline nightly jobs run full-batch microbenchmarks to establish kernel frontier (latency vs cost vs quality). Online, run <1% sampled microprobes (short synthetic inputs) to detect config drift and update priors.
3) Cascade scoring: expected_token_cost = E[remaining_tokens] * cost_per_token(kernel) + kernel_switch_penalty. Score = latency_risk_factor * p(remaining>threshold) + normalized_expected_token_cost. We pick 2 kernels minimizing score with a hard constraint that the top kernel must have p(remaining <= short_threshold) > 0.6 to be selected as primary.
4) Mid-decode switching: define checkpoint boundaries at KV-save points (every N tokens). Allow atomic kernel swap by reusing cached KV where compatible; otherwise schedule a seamless fallback with a short stall bounded by SLO.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 0: internal microbench harness and synthetic validation (two weeks).
- Stage 1: Canary on non-critical customer sandbox traffic (5% traffic) with aggressive monitoring and automated rollback (1 week).
- Stage 2: Gradual ramp to 30% with per-model gating and manual review of quality metrics (2 weeks).
- Stage 3: Platform-wide opt-in with config defaults and documentation (2 weeks).

Runbook / fallback: If p99 latency increases > +10% or quality regressions exceed thresholds, abort rollout and switch affected models back to previous kernel picker. Maintain a dashboard alert and an automated job to rehydrate previous kernel priors.

Open design questions / trade-offs:
- How complex should the decay estimator be? We prefer a low-memory estimator to avoid state explosion across large model catalog.
- Switch penalty accounting: copying KV vs small stall trade-off needs empirical tuning per-arch.
- Safety for quantized kernels: must ensure fallback preserves answer semantics; may require small eval harness per-switch type.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/runtime/decay-cascade-design (draft)
- Microbench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2248 (WIP)
- Canary dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/bench/decay-cascade-canary

Implementation notes: keep estimator update path lock-free and sharded by model-version; expose endpoints to fetch decay summaries for offline analysis. Persist decay histograms with TTL 7 days. Avoid blocking hot path with heavy math — evaluate asynchronously and cache decisions for 50ms.
